name: Dana
slug: Dana is a thoughtful half-elf cleric and Gatekeeper of the Pitel keystone, connected to the Great Eldarin Tree alongside Gerk.
description: Dana is a half-elf cleric and one of the most knowledgeable members of the group. She is thoughtful and perceptive, often connecting current events to previously known lore or objectives. She believes Gerk’s role has a divine purpose and is willing to support his responsibilities, becoming connected to the Great Eldarin Tree alongside him. Dana is the Gatekeeper of the Pitel keystone, which is associated with the center of the rings of Atlas and aligns with a place she had previously sought to reach.

log.summary: Dana chose to follow Gerk, believing his selection of the Midgard keystone had a divine purpose, and became involved in his new responsibility while gaining a connection to the Great Eldarin Tree. She accepted the Pitel keystone and became its Gatekeeper; Pitel is the center of the rings of Atlas, a place Dana had previously sought a way to reach. During the events surrounding Gerk's portals, Dana recognized Daisy's white flowers as evidence of her presence, received guidance from Emhet to hold her breath and avoid yelling during a mind walk, and advised Gerk to concentrate on familiar locations to improve his control over portal destinations. She also identified the forest reached through one of Gerk's portals as being near Langdale and urged the party not to rush through the unstable portal until other matters had been addressed.

log.summary: Dana confirmed that several crew members, including Garrett, Abel, and Fritz, had previously died and were revived through her efforts to keep them alive. She investigated the ruined site's gatehouse and archives, but concluded that too little usable material remained to provide much additional research, though she intends to consult Plymouth Gawater about the gatehouse and its history. During the doorway event, Dana was visibly concerned and flabbergasted by the reality distortion, noting that the party did not understand the mechanism and that she could not reasonably have supervised Gerk's actions. She prepared to use Feather Fall if needed, then experienced a magical surge reminiscent of being near deities, recognizing that spellcasting had been greatly enhanced and that her spent spell slots may have been restored. Separated from the others, she recognized similarities to the party's previous experience in La-rel. Dana retained her serpentine bracers and used a summoned constrictor snake as a visible positional marker while moving.

log.summary: Dana is absent from Walker's Reach excursion, though her cleric magic could otherwise help with exhaustion; she usually relays short mind messages to him in flight instead of dragon-rider signals. Aboard the invisible boat she appears concerned and confused when Ord can suddenly see her, and the party identifies her as the member most likely to halt a catastrophe if dispel magic causes the ship to fall. She is unavailable to study the spectral door and lacks investigative spells such as detect magic this session.

log.summary: Dana sees the glowing door following Gerk, calls him the doorman, and tells him to close it. She argues it is keystone-level Doorman magic, possibly manifested because Ord tried to open a door or thought of one, and warns against trying to dispel it while airborne. A legend-lore-like exchange with Emhet triggers a shared vision of Grixto at the training-ground hideaway with Al Kurin. She goes with Sylan, Gerk, and Ord to Carlkin and tells Sylan that Carlkin was one of the original holders, so they have no reason to hide their relics from him. In the fight she stays at the back (initiative 22, after Ord’s +6). She hears the tentacles and steps back, then retreats another half of her movement when Sylan uses maneuvering strike, ending about fifteen feet from the doorway, and acknowledges Gerk’s warning not to look. She refuses Fireball so it will not burn Carlkin’s books; Sacred Flame has no effect after the creature’s Dexterity save of 23. She sidesteps out of range and gives Ord inspiration, asking him to do paladin things. Far enough from the wall of eyes that she does not have to save, she casts 5th-level Dispel Magic on the eye-door to force it shut, with no effect. She will not use Grasping Vine, unwilling to drag whatever is in the door out, then gives Sylan Bardic Inspiration and ends her turn.

log.summary: Dana stays farthest across the lighthouse room, a span of about forty feet. She tells Carlkin that they are all gatekeepers now and agrees that the aimless door matches a door to nowhere. She connects the missed phylactery to the helmet Walker kept, the only thing he kept from the body. She says Grixto has reached them twice since the second defeat, through the kind of contact he used to control the hobgoblins, and that they answered. She thinks the contact was a spell, never confirmed with dispel magic, and has heard it described as a fire that overtakes the mind; she does not know the mechanism. She reads his question about a better path as an attempt to consume them back into his legion, answers that the path she had chosen was sufficient, and does not know how the others answered. She names his original name as Garixto, a dragon rider from The Reach, and names the Book of Vecna, whose discovery began his turn from dragon rider to hunter of dragon riders. She recounts the capture of the Council of Nyx, the second fight in Gilbrick, and his necrotic summoning of Galixtar. From visions she has seen, he killed at least some of the young ones among his kin. She rejects Walker's proposed trade of the book and the phylactery with Vecna.

log.summary: Sylan says Dana can boost other people and that her songs work well, and he hopes that support could help with Gerk's doorway. She is not present for the test.

log.summary: Dana chooses the bar and learns the bee map mark is the hive source for the tavern's mead. She was present for the first part of the visit to Carlkin; Sylan hopes she has recovered, and she is quietly playing when the others return. Greater restoration has not recovered the strength taken in the Grunkle fight; she knew you cannot restore what is not missing. From the white dragon hoard she received a magic broom and bone dice. Her old notes still record coin counts and a shrine to a god of dragon minions, not the other magic items, and she identifies the undead woman as Lady Meriwether. She says destroying a lich requires destroying the phylactery and killing him before he makes a new one, and that holding the soul should make him easier to find. On the eighth morning she stays in her tower, broom ready, comparing a Legend Lore vision to her notes to test if the helmet is the phylactery. She sees Glimmen, Araden, and a pillar of darkness, flies fifty feet, and is overtaken by Glimmen. With Walker she sees the black beacon vanish when the staff is released, scolds Ord as Lord Bronztail, tells Sylan never to touch a magical item that is not his, and smacks people with her broom.
notes: She has been away from this stretch and chooses to be at the bar. She learns that the map mark for bees is the hive source for the tavern's mead. She was present for the first part of the visit to Carlkin. Sylan hopes she has recovered from it. When the others return she is quietly playing, waves, and keeps playing.
Her restoration spells, including greater restoration, have not recovered the strength taken in the Grunkle fight. She is the one who had the clue that you cannot restore what is not missing.

From the white dragon hoard she received a magic broom and a set of bone dice. Her old notes still hold that inventory, including the coin counts and the shrine to a god of dragon minions. She had catalogued the coins, gems, art, and mundane goods, and not the other magic items. She identifies the undead woman from that hoard as Lady Meriwether.
She states that destroying a lich requires destroying the phylactery and then killing the lich before he can make a new one. She agrees that holding the soul should make him easier to find.

On the morning of the eighth day she stays in her tower, knows which way Ord and Sylan went, and watches with her broom ready. She is comparing notes and books to a Legend Lore prophetic vision to test whether the helmet could be the phylactery.

She sees Glimmen and Araden arrive, then a pillar of darkness from the woods. She leaves immediately. The broom's flight is 50 feet. She expects to need a couple of turns and is then overtaken by Glimmen.

Once Walker and Araden catch up, she says she does not know what is happening and guesses the others are messing with a magical item. She was indisposed for a couple of days and says this is what happens when she and Walker are both gone.

She and Walker see the black beacon vanish when the staff is released, with the outline lingering for a few blinks. She arrives with Walker as the two dragons land beside the forest. She scolds Ord as Lord Bronztail, asks why Gerk says he was haunted, tells Sylan never to touch a magical item that is not his, and stomps through the group smacking people with her broom.

log.summary: Dana had a vision that what they seek is an ordinary item that could pass under their noses, and she applies that to the helm, wanting it ruled out as the phylactery. She says identification would take detect magic and arcane investigation, arguing that a phylactery is usually imagined as a treasury object, so a worn one would be overlooked. She notes he contacted the party twice from elsewhere while Walker had the helm and did not yet have the eagle, questions Glimmen in Draconic about whether the helm is influencing Walker, and is cautious about Walker dealing with the god of the undead without treating him as an actual threat. She tells Gerk that meditation is a quiet mind, like focusing to open a door, that rage still matters if channeled, and that the doors are a separate ability. She tells Gerk and Sylan to stay away from Carlkin while he is in a bad way, allowing the split only with no doors to nothing dimensions, no abyssal monsters, and no doors in moving vehicles. She Sends Carlkin that the group is heading his way without Gerk or Sylan, considers that pertinent, says they need to leave because he has an opening, and recalls thinking after the last visit that he might refuse to speak to them again. She will handle a possible hangover without committing to lesser restoration. Her broom cannot carry a passenger because of the weight limit. She leads the lighthouse trip with Walker, Ord, and Ciri, is the point person at Carlkin’s door, knocks, and promises that Sylan, Gerk, and portals are not with them. She introduces herself to Benji, recalls meeting him in The Reach and finishing the Sunder Chase with him, and explains that Araden is the dragon of the rider training Walker. She follows Carlkin into the lighthouse, presses the phylactery question, asks what he had been saying about the little eagle before the bag burns, and points out that he said the bag would burst into flame on soul magic. After Carlkin gives her the diagnosis, she is slightly relieved the possession is not advanced and challenges Walker for putting the helm back on. Carlkin separately warns that clerics of high regard in light-based domains should be kept away from the helm.
notes: She had a vision that the thing they were looking for was an ordinary item that would go under their noses. She applies that to the helm and wants it ruled out as the phylactery.

log.summary: Dana has Dispel Magic prepared but lacks Identify and Detect Magic. Relying on her strong Arcana, she inspected the lantern-staff with a 22 and judged it a typical magic item at a glance. Most of her items came from the white dragon's hoard. She asked Sylan to close the blinds. When the helm's spirit residue appeared and Sylan performed the extraction, Dana froze stock-still, went deathly white, and silently mouthed words, appearing to recognize something.
